sections.title: Databricks Intelligence Platform
sections.weightHint: Architecture, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, compute & cost
objectives: Understand the core components of the Data Intelligence Platform (architecture, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog)
Understand the compute services, their characteristics, limits and cost models, and pick the right one per workload
sections.notes:
Core components

  • Lakehouse architecture — open Delta/Parquet data in cloud storage, unifying engineering, analytics, ML and AI under one governance layer.
  • Delta Lake — the table format: ACID transactions, time travel (query past versions), schema enforcement, and the transaction log.
  • Unity Catalog (UC) — the governance layer: a three-level namespace catalog.schema.table, permissions, automatic lineage, and audit.

Compute services & cost

  • All-purpose compute — interactive dev in notebooks; stays up; most expensive if left idle.
  • Job compute — created for an automated job and torn down after; cheaper for scheduled work.
  • SQL warehouse — for SQL/BI queries and dashboards.
  • Serverless vs classic — serverless is managed & auto-optimized by Databricks with fast startup; classic runs in your cloud account.
  • Billing is measured in DBUs (per-second). Rule of thumb: scheduled pipeline → job/serverless; interactive exploration → all-purpose; BI dashboard → SQL warehouse.
videos: Databricks Data Intelligence Platform architecture overview
Databricks Delta Lake Unity Catalog explained
Compute types & when to use them
Databricks compute all purpose vs job vs SQL warehouse serverless

quiz.q: A team needs reliable rollbacks after bad ingests, audit trails for regulatory compliance, and one consistent source of truth for both AI and BI. Which strategy fits best?
opts: Store CSVs in DBFS with nightly copies for manual rollback
Use Delta Lake ACID transactions and time travel, governed by Unity Catalog
Query raw files in cloud object storage ad hoc and recover from backups
Keep data in in-memory DataFrames for audit and BI
quiz.obj: Value of the platform / Delta Lake + Unity Catalog
quiz.e: Delta Lake gives ACID transactions and time travel (rollback + history); Unity Catalog governs access and lineage for a single AI/BI source of truth.

quiz.q: Many analysts run ad hoc SQL on curated Delta tables all day. You need fast startup, many concurrent users, and cost control (no oversized clusters). Best compute?
opts: A job cluster with autoscaling built for scheduled ETL
An all-purpose cluster with a fixed number of workers
A single-node cluster for lightweight dev
quiz.obj: Select the right compute for a workload
quiz.e: A serverless SQL warehouse is purpose-built for concurrent SQL/BI with fast startup and elastic scaling.

quiz.q: An engineer accidentally overwrote a Delta table with bad data. What is the fastest way to recover the prior state?
opts: Restore the table to a previous version using Delta time travel
Delete the table and rebuild from a nightly CSV backup
Enlarge the cluster and re-run the job
quiz.e: Delta's transaction log lets you time travel / RESTORE to a previous version instantly.

quiz.q: A nightly ETL job runs on an always-on all-purpose cluster. The team wants to cut cost without changing the logic. Best change?
opts: Run it on job compute that starts and terminates with the run
Move it to a SQL warehouse
Add autoscaling to the always-on cluster
quiz.e: Job compute is provisioned per run and torn down after, eliminating idle cost.

quiz.q: An organization wants one governance layer for permissions, lineage, and audit across all workspaces. Which component provides this?
quiz.e: Unity Catalog centralizes governance (permissions, lineage, audit) across the account.

quiz.q: An engineer on a legacy no-isolation cluster can't see any Unity Catalog catalogs. What should they do?
opts: Switch to a Unity-Catalog-enabled access mode (Standard or Dedicated)
Grant ALL PRIVILEGES on the metastore
quiz.e: UC requires a supported access mode — Standard (shared) or Dedicated (single-user); legacy no-isolation compute can't access UC.

quiz.q: An append fails because the incoming DataFrame has an unexpected extra column. What most likely caused the failure?
opts: Delta schema enforcement rejected the mismatched columns
quiz.e: Schema enforcement blocks writes whose columns don't match the table schema (evolution would instead adapt it).

quiz.q: A scheduled pipeline should run on compute that starts fast and needs no cluster sizing or tuning. Best option?
opts: A SQL warehouse for arbitrary Python ETL
quiz.e: Serverless is managed and auto-optimized with fast startup — no sizing/tuning.

quiz.q: How does Databricks bill compute consumption?
opts: A flat monthly fee per user
In DBUs, billed per second by compute type
quiz.e: Usage is measured in DBUs on a per-second, pay-as-you-go basis.

quiz.q: Which statement best describes the value of the lakehouse architecture?
opts: It requires separate data lake and warehouse systems
It unifies engineering, BI and AI on open formats under one governance layer
It stores data in a closed proprietary format
It removes the need for compute
quiz.obj: Value of the Data Intelligence Platform
quiz.e: The lakehouse unifies workloads on open Delta/Parquet governed by Unity Catalog.

quiz.q: A scheduled PySpark ETL job (not SQL) needs the cheapest, isolated compute. Which fits?
opts: A shared all-purpose cluster left running
Job compute provisioned for the run
quiz.e: Job compute is isolated per run and cheaper than an always-on interactive cluster; SQL warehouses are for SQL, not arbitrary PySpark.

quiz.q: Which technology adds ACID transactions and time travel on top of Parquet files?
quiz.e: Delta Lake layers a transaction log over Parquet to provide ACID and time travel.

flashcards: Lakehouse
Open Delta/Parquet data in cloud storage unifying engineering, analytics, ML and AI under one governance layer.
Delta Lake
Table format giving ACID transactions, time travel, and schema enforcement via a transaction log.
Unity Catalog
Governance layer with a 3-level namespace (catalog.schema.table), permissions, lineage and audit.
All-purpose vs job compute
All-purpose = interactive, stays up; job = spun up per run and torn down (cheaper for schedules).
SQL warehouse
Compute purpose-built for SQL and BI dashboards.
Serverless vs classic
Serverless is Databricks-managed and auto-optimized with fast startup; classic runs in your cloud account.
DBU
Databricks Unit — the per-second measure of compute consumption used for billing.

sections.title: Data Ingestion & Loading
sections.weightHint: COPY INTO, Auto Loader, Lakeflow Connect, JDBC/REST, JSON
objectives: Enable batch, streaming and incremental ingestion from sources like local files and Lakeflow Connect connectors
Use COPY INTO to incrementally load files from cloud storage into UC tables
Use Auto Loader with schema enforcement and evolution (directory listing / file notification)
Configure Lakeflow Connect to ingest from enterprise sources into UC tables
Use JDBC/ODBC or REST clients in notebooks to land data, orchestrated by Lakeflow Jobs
Prioritize between Auto Loader, Lakeflow Connect and other methods by volume, frequency, types and governance
Ingest semi-structured/unstructured data (e.g. nested JSON) into UC-governed Delta tables
sections.notes:
COPY INTO

SQL command that incrementally loads files from cloud object storage (S3/ADLS/GCS) into a UC table. It is idempotent — re-running skips files already loaded, so it's safe to retry.

COPY INTO my_catalog.sales.bronze
FROM 's3://bucket/landing/'
FILEFORMAT = JSON;

Auto Loader

  • Uses the cloudFiles source to incrementally pick up new files as they arrive.
  • Two file-detection modes: directory listing and file notification (event-based, better at scale).
  • Supports schema inference, enforcement and evolution via a schema location; tracks progress with a checkpoint.

Lakeflow Connect

Managed connectors that reliably ingest from enterprise sources (SaaS apps, databases) into UC tables with little code; standard connectors cover common formats/sources.

Choosing a method & other clients

  • Auto Loader → continuous files landing in cloud storage. Lakeflow Connect → managed pulls from enterprise systems. COPY INTO → simple incremental SQL loads.
  • JDBC/ODBC or REST clients in notebooks can land data too, usually scheduled with Lakeflow Jobs.
  • Semi-structured JSON / nested data is ingested into Delta and flattened with functions like from_json and explode.
videos: Databricks COPY INTO tutorial incremental load
Databricks Auto Loader cloudFiles schema evolution file notification
Databricks Lakeflow Connect managed connectors ingestion

quiz.q: New JSON files land continuously in an S3 bucket and must be ingested incrementally as they arrive. Best approach?
opts: Run COPY INTO manually each morning
Use Auto Loader with the cloudFiles source
Re-read the whole bucket in a batch job each run
quiz.e: Auto Loader (cloudFiles) incrementally picks up new files as they arrive at scale.

quiz.q: Incoming JSON begins including new nullable columns. You want them added to the target automatically without manual edits. What should you configure?
opts: Disable inference and hardcode the schema
Auto Loader with a schema location so it evolves and adds new columns
Drop and recreate the table each run
quiz.e: Auto Loader with cloudFiles.schemaLocation supports schema evolution, adding new (nullable) columns as they appear.

quiz.q: Millions of files per hour arrive in ADLS and directory listing has become too slow. Which Auto Loader mode should you use?
quiz.e: File notification mode uses cloud events/queues and scales far beyond directory listing.

quiz.q: You need a SQL command that incrementally and idempotently loads files from cloud storage into a Unity Catalog table. Which is it?
opts: CREATE STREAMING TABLE from a view
quiz.e: COPY INTO loads incrementally and skips already-loaded files (idempotent).

quiz.q: A source occasionally overwrites and re-uploads a file. How can you still query historical versions of the ingested Delta table?
opts: Delta keeps prior versions — use time travel to query history
quiz.e: Delta retains prior table versions, so time travel can query earlier states even after overwrites.

quiz.q: You must ingest from a SaaS application and an operational database into UC tables with minimal custom code. Best tool?
quiz.e: Lakeflow Connect provides managed connectors for enterprise/SaaS sources into UC tables.

quiz.q: An Auto Loader stream restarts after a failure and must not reprocess files it already ingested. What makes this work?
opts: The checkpoint location tracks processed files
quiz.e: The checkpoint records processed files/offsets so a restart resumes without duplicates.

quiz.q: Incoming JSON has a nested array field and you need one output row per array element. Which function do you use?
quiz.e: explode() expands each element of an array into its own row.

quiz.q: Only a few small batches of files arrive occasionally and you want the simplest setup. Which Auto Loader mode is appropriate?
quiz.e: Directory listing needs no cloud-event setup and is fine for low file volumes.

quiz.q: You need COPY INTO to reload files it has already ingested (e.g., after fixing them). What do you set?
quiz.e: COPY INTO's force = true disables idempotency so previously-loaded files are reloaded.

quiz.q: Records with malformed or unexpected fields should be captured rather than silently dropped during Auto Loader ingestion. Where do they go?
quiz.e: Auto Loader routes data that doesn't match the schema into the _rescued_data column.

quiz.q: Your data already lands as files in cloud object storage (not a SaaS source) and arrives continuously. Which ingestion tool is the best default?
quiz.e: For files continuously landing in cloud storage, Auto Loader is the right tool; Lakeflow Connect targets enterprise sources.

flashcards: COPY INTO
SQL command that incrementally loads files from cloud storage into a UC table; idempotent (skips already-loaded files).
Auto Loader
Incrementally ingests new files via the cloudFiles source, with schema inference/enforcement/evolution.
Auto Loader modes
Directory listing vs file notification (event-based, better at large scale).
Lakeflow Connect
Managed/standard connectors that ingest from enterprise sources (SaaS, DBs) into UC tables with little code.
Schema evolution
Auto Loader adapts to new columns over time using a schema location.
explode() / from_json()
from_json parses JSON strings into structs; explode turns array elements into separate rows.
Choosing ingestion
Auto Loader = files in cloud storage; Lakeflow Connect = enterprise sources; COPY INTO = simple incremental SQL loads.

sections.title: Data Transformation & Modeling
sections.weightHint: Cleaning, joins, dedup/aggregates, tuning, Gold objects
objectives: Clean data: read bronze with PySpark/SQL, handle nulls, standardize types, write silver tables
Combine DataFrames: inner/left/broadcast/cross joins, multiple keys, union / union all
Manipulate columns/rows/structures: add, drop, split, rename, filter, explode arrays
Deduplicate and aggregate: count, approx_count_distinct, mean, summary
Understand tuning parameters and re-measure performance
Build Gold objects: materialized views, views, streaming tables and tables for BI
Apply data quality checks and validation rules for reliable Silver/Gold
sections.notes:
Cleaning (bronze → silver)

Read raw bronze, drop/replace nulls (na.drop, fillna), cast types (cast), standardize, then write trustworthy silver tables.

Joins & set operations

  • inner / left / cross joins; join on multiple keys.
  • Broadcast join — when one side is small enough to fit in memory, Spark ships it to every executor (controlled by spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold).
  • union/unionAll stack rows and keep duplicates — use distinct() to remove them.

Column/row ops & dedup/aggregates

  • withColumn, drop, split, withColumnRenamed, filter/where, explode.
  • dropDuplicates removes duplicate rows; count, approx_count_distinct (fast estimate of uniques), mean/avg, and summary()/describe().

Tuning parameters

  • spark.sql.shuffle.partitions — post-shuffle partition count. spark.default.parallelism — default RDD parallelism.
  • spark.executor.memory/spark.driver.memory; spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold — max size to auto-broadcast.

Gold layer objects

Table = stored data; View = query recomputed on read; Materialized view = precomputed, refreshed results; Streaming table = incremental ingest/transform.
videos: PySpark inner left broadcast join union tutorial
Views vs materialized views vs streaming tables
Databricks materialized view streaming table vs view

quiz.q: A huge fact table must be joined to a small dimension table. How do you avoid an expensive shuffle?
quiz.e: Broadcasting the small side ships it to all executors, avoiding a shuffle (governed by autoBroadcastJoinThreshold).

quiz.q: After union-ing two DataFrames you see duplicate rows. What is happening?
opts: union keeps duplicates — apply distinct() to remove them
quiz.e: In Spark, union/unionAll keep duplicates; use distinct() to dedup.

quiz.q: You need to turn each element of an array column into its own row. Which operation?
quiz.e: explode() expands array elements into separate rows.

quiz.q: You need a fast, approximate count of distinct users over billions of rows. Which function?
quiz.e: approx_count_distinct trades a little accuracy for speed on large data (HyperLogLog).

quiz.q: Which operation removes duplicate rows from a DataFrame?
quiz.e: dropDuplicates() removes duplicate rows (optionally on a subset of columns).

quiz.q: A BI team needs a Gold object that stores precomputed results and is refreshed (not recomputed on every query). What should you build?
quiz.e: A materialized view stores refreshed precomputed results; a plain view recomputes on read.

quiz.q: A declarative pipeline should DROP records that fail a quality rule but keep running. Which expectation clause?
opts: There is no way to handle bad rows
quiz.e: ON VIOLATION DROP ROW discards failing rows while the pipeline continues.

quiz.q: A pipeline must FAIL the run if a critical data-quality constraint is violated. Which clause?
quiz.e: ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE stops the pipeline update when the expectation is violated.

quiz.q: Cleaning bronze into silver, you must drop rows with nulls and standardize types before writing. Which approach?
opts: df.na.drop() and cast(), then write to the silver table
quiz.e: Use na.drop()/fillna and cast() to clean and conform, then write the trustworthy silver table.

quiz.q: Which PySpark expression returns the count of UNIQUE invoice ids per day?
quiz.e: count_distinct('inv_id') counts unique invoices; count() would include duplicates.

quiz.q: Which tuning parameter controls the number of partitions produced after a shuffle, and what is its default?
quiz.e: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions sets post-shuffle partition count; the default is 200.

quiz.q: A Gold object needs to ingest and transform data incrementally as it arrives. Which object type?
quiz.e: A streaming table processes data incrementally; materialized views recompute results.

flashcards: Broadcast join
Ships a small table to all executors to avoid a shuffle; controlled by spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold.
union / unionAll
Stack rows and KEEP duplicates; use distinct() to dedup.
explode()
Turns each element of an array column into its own row.
dropDuplicates()
Removes duplicate rows (optionally by a subset of columns).
approx_count_distinct
Fast approximate count of unique values for large data.
spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
Sets the number of partitions produced after a shuffle.
View vs materialized view vs streaming table
View recomputes on read; MV stores refreshed precomputed results; streaming table ingests incrementally.

sections.title: Working with Lakeflow Jobs
sections.weightHint: Control flow, tasks & DAG, triggers, scheduling
objectives: Implement control flow (retries, conditional/branching, looping) with Lakeflow Jobs
Configure tasks (notebook, SQL, dashboard, pipeline) and dependencies as a DAG
Implement schedules with trigger types: scheduled, file arrival, table update
Choose between time-based and data-driven triggers based on data availability
sections.notes:
Lakeflow Jobs

  • A job orchestrates tasks — notebook, SQL, dashboard, and pipeline tasks — with dependencies that form a DAG.
  • Control flow: automatic retries, conditional/if-else tasks (branching), and for-each loops over a set of inputs.
  • Repair run re-executes only the failed task(s), keeping successful results.

Triggers & scheduling

  • Scheduled (time-based / cron), file arrival (runs when new files land), and table update (runs when a table changes).
  • Time-based triggers fire on a clock; data-driven triggers (file arrival / table update) fire when data is actually ready — choose based on data availability and dependencies.
videos: Databricks Lakeflow Jobs tasks dependencies DAG tutorial
Triggers: scheduled, file arrival, table update
Databricks job trigger file arrival table update scheduled
Databricks Lakeflow Jobs conditional task for each loop retries

quiz.q: A cleanup task must always drop temp tables regardless of whether the upstream transform succeeded or failed. Which run_if condition?
quiz.e: ALL_DONE runs the task once all dependencies finish, regardless of their success/failure.

quiz.q: A reporting task should run only when every upstream task has succeeded (the default). Which run_if?
quiz.e: ALL_SUCCESS (the default) runs the task only if all dependencies succeed.

quiz.q: In a 3-task job (A→B→C), Task B fails. After fixing B's code, how do you resume without re-running Task A?
opts: Rerun the whole job from the start
Use Repair Run and select the failed task and its downstream task(s)
Trigger B and C as separate one-off jobs
Clone the job without Task A
quiz.e: Repair Run re-executes only the selected failed/downstream tasks, keeping A's successful output.

quiz.q: One task should start only after several independent upstream tasks all finish (fan-in). How do you configure it?
opts: Add all the upstream tasks as its dependencies
Put each upstream task in a separate job
quiz.e: Listing multiple upstream tasks as dependencies creates a fan-in in the DAG.

quiz.q: A job should launch automatically whenever new files land in a monitored location. Which trigger?
quiz.e: A file-arrival trigger is data-driven and fires when new files appear.

quiz.q: A job should run only when a specific source table is updated. Which trigger type?
quiz.e: A table-update trigger runs the job when the monitored table changes.

quiz.q: A pipeline must run every night at 02:00. Which trigger is appropriate?
quiz.e: A scheduled/cron trigger runs on a fixed clock time.

quiz.q: A custom JDBC ingestion notebook must run on a schedule as cheaply and reliably as possible. How should you operationalize it?
opts: Run it by hand on a shared all-purpose cluster
Schedule it as a job task on job compute
Leave an all-purpose cluster running 24/7 for it
Move it to a SQL warehouse
quiz.e: A scheduled job task on job compute is isolated and cost-efficient versus an interactive all-purpose cluster.

quiz.q: You need to run the same task once for each item in a list of inputs. Which construct?
quiz.e: A for-each task loops a task over an input array.

quiz.q: Part of the job's DAG should run only if a computed value meets a condition. Which construct?
quiz.e: An If/else condition task adds branching based on task values, parameters, or expressions.

quiz.q: How are the tasks and their dependencies in a Lakeflow Job organized?
opts: As a flat list run in parallel
quiz.e: Tasks with dependencies form a DAG-based task graph.

quiz.q: A task that calls a sometimes-flaky external API occasionally fails transiently. What should you configure?
quiz.e: Automatic retries recover from transient failures without manual reruns.

flashcards: Lakeflow Jobs
Orchestrates notebook/SQL/dashboard/pipeline tasks with dependencies as a DAG.
DAG
The directed acyclic task graph formed by a job's tasks and their dependencies.
Repair run
Reruns only the failed task(s) of a job, keeping successful results.
Trigger types
Scheduled (time), file arrival, and table update (data-driven).
Time-based vs data-driven
Time-based fires on a clock; data-driven fires when files land or a table updates.
Conditional & for-each tasks
Conditional/if-else adds branching; for-each loops a task over inputs.

sections.title: Implementing CI/CD
sections.weightHint: Git in workspace, Asset Bundles, targets, Databricks CLI
objectives: Manage code in the workspace: branches, commit/push, pull requests via Databricks Git
Understand environment config with Asset Bundle variables and overrides across dev/test/prod
Deploy Asset Bundles to package and promote jobs, pipelines and assets across environments
Understand the Databricks CLI to validate, deploy and manage bundles in CI/CD
sections.notes:
Git in the workspace

Databricks Git folders (Repos) integrate Git: create and switch branches, commit and push, and open pull requests through the Git provider — standard dev workflow inside the workspace.

Asset Bundles (Automation Bundles)

  • Infrastructure-as-code in YAML (databricks.yml): define resources (jobs, pipelines) and targets (per-environment).
  • Variables and overrides let one codebase promote across dev → test → prod targets.
targets:
  dev:  { mode: development }
  prod: { mode: production }

Databricks CLI

  • databricks bundle validate — check the bundle config.
  • databricks bundle deploy — deploy/promote the bundle to a target.
videos: Databricks Repos Git folders branches pull request tutorial
Databricks Asset Bundles databricks.yml targets variables tutorial
Databricks CLI bundle validate deploy tutorial

quiz.q: A team wants a modular way to version, deploy, and orchestrate ETL pipelines with CI/CD and repeatability. Which feature fits?
opts: Represent jobs as Unity Catalog models and promote via aliases
Package logic as wheels in Volumes bound to tasks
Rely on notebook revision history for versioning
Use Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs), versioned in Git and promoted via automated CI/CD
quiz.e: DABs define resources + code as YAML, are version-controlled in Git, and promote across environments via CI/CD.

quiz.q: Where are per-environment (dev/staging/prod) configurations defined in a bundle?
quiz.e: targets hold environment-specific configuration and overrides in databricks.yml.

quiz.q: In a pull-request pipeline you want to check a bundle's configuration WITHOUT deploying it. Which command?
quiz.e: databricks bundle validate checks the configuration; deploy is used to actually deploy.

quiz.q: A CI job must deploy a bundle non-interactively (no manual confirmation). Which flag?
quiz.e: --auto-approve lets the deploy proceed without interactive confirmation in automation.

quiz.q: You want a deploy to fail rather than disrupt a job that is currently running. Which flag helps?
quiz.e: --fail-on-active-runs makes the deploy fail if there are active runs, protecting them.

quiz.q: Within Databricks Git folders, what can a developer do?
opts: Create/switch branches, commit and push, and open pull requests
quiz.e: Git folders support branching, commit/push, and PRs through the Git provider.

quiz.q: When are Databricks Asset Bundle variables resolved?
opts: At deployment time (statically), not at runtime
quiz.e: Bundle variables/overrides are resolved statically at deploy time, not dynamically at runtime.

quiz.q: How do you promote the SAME codebase across dev → staging → prod with a bundle?
opts: Copy notebooks between workspaces by hand
Use bundle targets with variable overrides
quiz.e: Targets plus variable overrides let one bundle deploy to each environment.

quiz.q: What is the root configuration file of a Databricks Asset Bundle?
quiz.e: databricks.yml is the bundle's root YAML config.

quiz.q: In a bundle, where are the jobs and pipelines themselves defined?
quiz.e: resources define jobs/pipelines; targets hold per-environment overrides.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of DABs over configuring jobs by clicking in the UI?
quiz.e: DABs are IaC: reproducible and promotable across environments, unlike ad-hoc UI clicks.

quiz.q: Which command deploys a validated bundle to a target environment?
quiz.e: databricks bundle deploy deploys/promotes the bundle to the chosen target.

flashcards: Databricks Git folders (Repos)
Git integration in the workspace: branches, commit/push, and pull requests.
Asset Bundles
YAML infrastructure-as-code (databricks.yml) defining resources and targets.
targets
Bundle section holding per-environment (dev/test/prod) config and overrides.
Bundle variables/overrides
Let one codebase be promoted across dev → test → prod.
databricks bundle deploy
CLI command that deploys/promotes a bundle to a target.
databricks bundle validate
CLI command that checks a bundle's configuration before deploy.

sections.title: Troubleshooting, Monitoring & Optimization
sections.weightHint: Run history, Spark UI, skew/shuffle/spill, Liquid Clustering
objectives: Identify job performance trends using Lakeflow Jobs run history vs baselines
Use the Lakeflow Jobs UI to monitor pipeline health (statuses, DAG, run times, failures)
Identify bottlenecks — skew, shuffling, disk spill — from Spark UI stage metrics
Understand Liquid Clustering and predictive optimization
Diagnose cluster startup failures, library conflicts and out-of-memory issues
sections.notes:
Monitoring jobs

  • Run history compares current execution times against historical baselines to spot regressions.
  • The Jobs UI shows statuses, the DAG (to find upstream blockers), run times and failure rates.

Spark UI bottlenecks

  • Skew — one task far slower than the rest (uneven data distribution).
  • Shuffle — data moved across the cluster; heavy shuffle is costly.
  • Spill — not enough memory, so data is written to disk (slow).

Layout optimization

  • Liquid Clustering — auto-manages data layout on chosen keys (replaces manual partitioning + ZORDER).
  • Predictive optimization — Databricks auto-runs OPTIMIZE (compaction) and VACUUM (cleanup).

Common failures

Cluster startup failures (quota/config), library conflicts (incompatible versions), and out-of-memory (reduce partition size, increase memory, avoid huge collects) — read driver/executor logs and the event log.
videos: Reading the Spark UI (skew, shuffle, spill)
Databricks Spark UI skew shuffle spill tutorial
Databricks Lakeflow Jobs run history monitor health tutorial

quiz.q: A batch job's runtime doubled. In the Spark UI one task takes 10 min while others finish in 30 s, and Max shuffle read (5 GB) is far above the median (400 MB). What's the simplest fix that needs no code change?
opts: Add more executors so the slow task finishes faster
Confirm Adaptive Query Execution skew-join handling is enabled to split the oversized partition at runtime
Lower spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to use fewer tasks
quiz.obj: Identify bottlenecks (skew) in the Spark UI
quiz.e: The metrics indicate data skew; AQE skew-join handling automatically splits the oversized partition without code changes. Bigger clusters don't fix skew.

quiz.q: AQE alone isn't resolving a severe skew on one hot join key. Which manual technique redistributes it?
opts: Salt the skewed join key to spread it across partitions
quiz.e: Salting the skewed key distributes its rows across partitions so no single task is overloaded.

quiz.q: The Spark UI shows large 'spill' during a stage. What does that indicate?
opts: Tasks ran out of memory and wrote data to disk
quiz.e: Spill means insufficient memory forced Spark to write to disk, slowing the job.

quiz.q: You suspect a job is slower than its usual baseline. Where do you confirm the regression?
opts: Compare the Lakeflow Jobs run history against historical baselines
quiz.e: Run history compares current execution times against historical baselines to surface regressions.

quiz.q: You want OPTIMIZE and VACUUM maintenance to run automatically without scheduling them. What enables this?
quiz.e: Predictive optimization automatically runs compaction (OPTIMIZE) and cleanup (VACUUM).

quiz.q: A large table's layout needs ongoing tuning on frequently filtered keys, hands-off, as it grows. Which feature?
opts: Manual partitioning + ZORDER on every write
quiz.e: Liquid Clustering auto-manages the layout on chosen keys, replacing manual partitioning + ZORDER.

quiz.q: A job repeatedly fails with out-of-memory errors on executors. A reasonable first step is to:
opts: Collect the whole DataFrame to the driver
Reduce data per task / add memory and avoid large driver collects
Move it to a SQL warehouse
quiz.e: Address OOM by shrinking per-task data, adding memory, and avoiding huge driver-side collects.

quiz.q: A cluster fails to start. What should you investigate first?
opts: It must be a code bug
The cluster event log for quota, config, or instance-availability issues
quiz.e: Startup failures usually stem from cloud quota/config/availability — check the event log.

quiz.q: After a library upgrade, a previously-working job now errors on import. Most likely cause?
opts: A library/version conflict — pin or resolve versions
quiz.e: Incompatible library versions cause conflicts; pin/resolve versions to fix.

quiz.q: Heavy 'shuffle' in a stage means what is happening?
opts: Data is being moved across the cluster between stages
A masked column is being read
quiz.e: Shuffle is cross-cluster data movement between stages; heavy shuffle is costly.

quiz.q: Where do you read stage-level metrics to diagnose skew, shuffle, and spill?
quiz.e: The Spark UI exposes per-stage/task metrics for diagnosing performance bottlenecks.

quiz.q: A multi-task pipeline is stuck; you need to find which upstream task is blocking it. What helps?
quiz.e: The DAG view shows task dependencies so you can spot the upstream blocker.

flashcards: Data skew
One task far slower than others due to uneven data distribution across partitions.
Shuffle
Movement of data across the cluster between stages; heavy shuffle is expensive.
Spill
Writing data to disk because memory ran out — a performance red flag.
Run history
Compares a job's current run times against historical baselines to spot regressions.
Liquid Clustering
Auto-manages table layout on chosen keys, replacing manual partitioning + ZORDER.
Predictive optimization
Databricks automatically runs OPTIMIZE (compaction) and VACUUM (cleanup).
OOM / library conflicts
Diagnose via driver/executor logs; fix OOM with more memory / smaller partitions, resolve version conflicts.

sections.title: Governance & Security
objectives: Differentiate managed vs external tables and perform operations (create/modify/delete/convert)
Configure access controls via UI and SQL: GRANT, REVOKE, DENY to principals across the hierarchy
Understand column-level masking and row-level security to restrict visibility by group
Understand Unity Catalog ABAC policies for central row filtering and column masking
sections.notes:
Managed vs external tables

  • Managed — UC manages metadata and data files; DROP deletes the data.
  • External — data lives in a location you specify; UC manages only metadata; DROP keeps the data. Tables can be converted between the two.

Access control

  • GRANT gives a privilege, REVOKE removes a previously-granted one, DENY explicitly blocks it.
  • Privileges apply to principals — users, groups, and service principals — at levels of the hierarchy (catalog / schema / table). Reading a table needs USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT.

Masking, row-level security & ABAC

  • Column masking — obscure sensitive column values for some users. Row-level security — a row filter limits which rows a group can see.
  • ABAC policies (attribute-based access control) in UC centrally apply row filters and column masks based on attributes/tags, instead of per-table rules.

quiz.q: An analyst group already has USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on sales. They now need read-only access to a table. Which grant?
quiz.e: SELECT gives read-only access; MODIFY/INSERT/ALL add write capability.

quiz.q: A user was mistakenly given write access. How do you remove that previously-granted privilege?
quiz.e: REVOKE removes a privilege that was granted (DENY explicitly blocks).

quiz.q: You DROP an EXTERNAL Unity Catalog table. What happens to the underlying data files?
opts: They remain in cloud storage (UC managed only metadata)
quiz.e: Dropping an external table leaves the data files; only the metadata is removed.

quiz.q: You want Unity Catalog to fully manage an existing external Delta table (so future maintenance and DROP behavior match managed tables). Which command?
opts: DROP TABLE t then CREATE it as external
quiz.e: ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED converts an external Delta table to a Unity Catalog managed table.

quiz.q: Analysts in different regions should each only see rows for their own region in a shared table. Which UC feature?
quiz.e: A row filter restricts which rows each user/group can see.

quiz.q: Some users must see a masked version of a sensitive column (e.g., last 4 digits only). Which feature?
quiz.e: A column mask returns an obscured value for users who shouldn't see the raw data.

quiz.q: You want to centrally apply row filters and column masks across many tables based on tags, rather than per table. Which UC feature?
quiz.e: ABAC policies use governed tags to apply row filters and column masks centrally across catalogs/schemas.

quiz.q: An automated pipeline (not a person) needs governed access to a table. Which principal should you grant to?
quiz.e: Automated workloads should use a service principal, one of UC's principal types (users, groups, service principals).

quiz.q: A group should read exactly one schema and nothing else in the catalog. Which grants follow least privilege?
opts: GRANT SELECT on the entire catalog
GRANT USE CATALOG, then USE SCHEMA + SELECT on just that schema
quiz.e: Grant USE CATALOG plus USE SCHEMA and SELECT scoped to the single schema — not catalog-wide privileges.

quiz.q: You DROP a MANAGED Unity Catalog table. What happens to the data?
quiz.e: For managed tables UC owns the data, so DROP deletes the underlying files.

quiz.q: Auditors ask who accessed a table and when. Where is this recorded?
opts: In Unity Catalog audit logs (system tables / delivered to cloud storage)
quiz.e: UC records who-did-what in audit logs, queryable via system tables and delivered to storage.

quiz.q: How does Unity Catalog obtain table- and column-level lineage?
opts: It is captured automatically as queries run across notebooks, jobs and dashboards
quiz.e: UC captures lineage automatically as queries execute.

flashcards: Managed vs external table
Managed: UC owns data, DROP deletes it. External: data in your location, DROP keeps it.
GRANT / REVOKE / DENY
GRANT gives a privilege, REVOKE removes a granted one, DENY explicitly blocks it.
Principals
Who privileges are granted to: users, groups, and service principals.
Row-level security
A row filter restricting which rows a user/group can see.
Column masking
Obscures sensitive column values for certain users/groups.
ABAC policies
Attribute/tag-based policies that centrally apply row filters and column masks in UC.
